reason: This passage from Exodus 14 describes Yahweh actively saving and defending the Israelites from the pursuing Egyptians. The text explicitly shows Yahweh fighting for the people (יְהוָה יִלָּחֵם לָכֶם - 'Yahweh will fight for you'), demonstrating divine protection and loyalty. The passage concludes with Israel witnessing 'the great hand' (הַיָּד הַגְּדֹלָה) that Yahweh performed on their behalf, leading them to fear Yahweh and believe in Him. There is no indication whatsoever that Yahweh considers not owing loyalty or replacing Israel with another people. The narrative demonstrates the opposite: active divine loyalty and covenant commitment.
